subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & tiering (Redwood Inference)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: multi-tenancy controls & tiering (Redwood Inference)

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the time today. As promised, here’s a short recap from our call and the proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- No clear per-customer rate limiting or quota system today; bursts from a few tenants are causing queueing and latency for others.
- Difficulty enforcing per-tenant routing/policies across models and regions (engineering overhead).
- Need to support tiered SLAs (free/standard/premium) with different throughput/latency guarantees.
- Security/compliance is important (SOC 2 audit upcoming); procurement will want artifacts.

Current stack:
- In-house service that front-ends a mix of hosted LLM APIs and some self-hosted model endpoints.
- Central auth + account service; no dedicated inference gateway for tenancy controls.

Success criteria for POC (what success looks like):
1) Demonstrate per-tenant rate limits and quotas enforced at the inference gateway level (min config: token/sec + concurrent requests per tenant).
2) Show policy-based routing so premium tenants hit dedicated capacity and fallback to standard when needed.
3) Measure 95th perc latency improvement under mixed-tenant load during a 24h soak.
4) Deliver SOC 2 summary and architecture notes for procurement.

Recommended next steps (we can do these in parallel):
- Redwood: share SOW draft + SOC 2 summary (attached).
- Redwood: set up short demo for your SRE team to walk through per-tenant routing and quota config — 45m.
- Acme: confirm ideal POC tenants (1 premium, 2 standard, 1 free) and available load windows.
- Acme: loop in procurement (contact details?) and share any constraints on billing/PO timing.

Tentative timeline:
- Week 1: SOW + SOC2 docs, scheduling demo
- Week 2: Demo + configuration workshop with SRE
- Week 3: 1-week POC with traffic shaping

Attachments: SOW-draft.pdf (SOW outline for POC), SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level artifacts).

If this looks right I’ll send the SOW and get the demo scheduled for next week.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks, Ben — this is helpful and aligned with what we discussed. A few quick notes:  

- Confirming pain: our peaks are driven by campaign kicks and a small set of partners that run batch jobs against our endpoints. Those spikes are the biggest blocker.
- For the POC tenants: I can nominate 1 premium (internal analytics), 2 standard (two mid-size merchant partners), and 1 free (dev sandbox).
- Procurement: please include our procurement team on the SOW. I’m copying procurement@acme.com — they’ll want net-30 and a short list of SOC 2 artifacts.
- Timeline: next week demo works for SRE (Wed/Thu mornings PST).

Question: can Redwood show both token/sec limits and concurrent request caps in the demo? We’d like to see how throttling vs queuing behaves. Also interested in policy-based routing rules (region + tier) — if you can show the fallback path that’d be great.

If you can share the SOW and SOC2 summary today I’ll get procurement eyes on it.

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform, Acme Retail
alex.johnson@acme.com
